name: Maxine D. Brown
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Birth year is not documented in reviewed sources; her defining contribution was co-editing the 1987 NSF report Visualization in Scientific Computing and work as EVL associate director from 1986 onward, both mid-career activities without a dated ≤26 breakout.
early_history_summary: Brown holds a B.A. in mathematics from Temple University and an M.S. in computer science from the University of Pennsylvania. She worked in technical communications and graphics software at Hewlett-Packard, ISSCO Graphics, and Digital Productions before joining the Electronic Visualization Laboratory at UIC in 1986.
evidence_summary: Brown is a significant figure in scientific visualization and advanced networking demos (iGrid, GLIF), but no verifiable birth year or material dated milestone at or before age 26 was found in reviewed sources. Career prominence begins with EVL and the 1987 NSF visualization report.

name: Jeremy Howard
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Fastmail (and Optimal Decisions Group) in 1999 at age 25, launching a premium paid email service that pioneered consumer IMAP features and later sold to Opera Software.
early_history_summary: Born in London and raised in Melbourne after moving there in 1976; attended Melbourne Grammar and studied philosophy at the University of Melbourne. He spent roughly eight years in management consulting at McKinsey & Co and A.T. Kearney before co-founding Fastmail and Optimal Decisions Group in 1999.
family_context_summary: Born in London; family relocated to Melbourne in 1976. Attended elite Melbourne Grammar School. Family financial status not documented beyond private-school attendance.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Melbourne Grammar, McKinsey consulting path, open-source Perl/IMAP, Fastmail cofounders
evidence_summary: Howard combined elite Australian secondary education and multi-year strategy consulting with hands-on open-source email systems work, then co-founded Fastmail and ODG in 1999 at about age 25. Cofounders Rob Mueller and Bruce Davey provided complementary technical depth. Later he became a top Kaggle competitor, Kaggle president/chief scientist, Enlitic founder, and fast.ai co-founder, but the ≤26 material milestone is the 1999 dual founding.
starting_point: Born in London in 1973; moved to Melbourne in 1976; attended Melbourne Grammar and later studied philosophy at the University of Melbourne.
current_position: Co-founder of fast.ai and deep learning educator/researcher; also associated with Answer.AI; continues public research, teaching, and open-source software work.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Fastmail and Optimal Decisions Group in Melbourne.
Optimal Decisions Group acquired by ChoicePoint, marking a successful exit from insurance analytics.
Became a top-ranked Kaggle competitor; later served as Kaggle president and chief scientist.
Fastmail acquired by Opera Software (later returned to independence via staff buyout).
Founded Enlitic to apply deep learning to medical imaging diagnostics.
Co-founded fast.ai with Rachel Thomas to democratize deep learning education and research.
Published ULMFiT, an influential transfer-learning method for NLP.

name: Charles Hoskinson
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Ethereum in late 2013 as one of the original founders and briefly served as CEO before departing in 2014 after a dispute over nonprofit vs. commercial structure; age ~25–26.
early_history_summary: Born 5 November 1987 on Maui, Hawaii. Attended Metropolitan State University of Denver and the University of Colorado Boulder studying mathematics without completing a degree. In 2013 he left consulting to run the Bitcoin Education Project, then joined Vitalik Buterin and others to found Ethereum.
family_context_summary: Born on Maui; later associated with Colorado and Wyoming. Father and brother are physicians who later co-opened a health clinic with him; early family wealth not clearly documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father is a physician (with brother also a physician); medical domain rather than crypto/tech, so limited direct domain transfer to blockchain founding.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early crypto community, Ethereum founding team, Bitcoin Education Project
evidence_summary: Hoskinson entered crypto via the Bitcoin Education Project in 2013 and joined the original Ethereum founding group with Vitalik Buterin at age ~25–26, briefly as CEO. After leaving over governance philosophy, he co-founded IOHK with Jeremy Wood and built Cardano. Family medical background is documented later but not as an early crypto advantage; the primary early edge was immersion in the 2013 crypto founder network during a structural wave.
starting_point: Born 5 November 1987 on Maui, Hawaii; later studied mathematics in Colorado without completing a degree; family includes physicians (father and brother).
current_position: Founder of Cardano and CEO/founder of Input Output (IOHK/IOG); crypto entrepreneur and Wyoming-based philanthropist with large ranch holdings; Forbes once estimated wealth in the mid-hundreds of millions.

trajectory.event: Launched Bitcoin Education Project and co-founded Ethereum as one of five original founders, briefly serving as CEO.
Left Ethereum after nonprofit-vs-commercial dispute; co-founded IOHK with Jeremy Wood.
Cardano mainnet and ADA cryptocurrency launched as IOHK's flagship public blockchain.
Forbes estimated personal wealth at roughly $500–600 million amid crypto boom.
Donated $20 million to Carnegie Mellon to establish the Hoskinson Center for Formal Mathematics.
Launched Wyoming Integrity PAC and increased involvement in state crypto policy.

name: Maciej Cegłowski
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Graduated Middlebury College in 1997 (age ~22) and later worked at Yahoo Brickhouse; Pinboard was founded in 2009 at age ~34, which is the career-defining product.
early_history_summary: Born in Warsaw in 1975 and immigrated to the U.S. at age six with his mother. Studied Russian, French, and studio art at Middlebury College (BA 1997), then worked as a backend engineer and community manager at Yahoo before launching Pinboard as a solo paid bookmarking service.
family_context_summary: Born in Warsaw; immigrated to the U.S. at age six with his mother. Family financial background not detailed in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Cegłowski is known for Pinboard (2009) and influential essays on privacy and the web, but no material independently verifiable milestone occurred by age 26. Early career was education and ordinary software engineering roles.

name: Nina Amenta
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Graduated Yale in classical civilization in 1979 (~age 20–21), then worked over a decade as a programmer before a Berkeley PhD in 1994 (~age 35–36); research fame came in the late 1990s surface-reconstruction work.
early_history_summary: Grew up in Pittsburgh exploring mathematical patterns inspired by M.C. Escher. Earned a Yale BA in classical civilization (1979), worked more than ten years as a computer programmer including medical ultrasound firmware, then re-entered academia via UC Berkeley and completed a PhD under Raimund Seidel in 1994.
family_context_summary: Grew up in Pittsburgh; family financial and professional background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Amenta became a leading computational geometry researcher (surface reconstruction, power crust) after a nontraditional path back to a PhD at ~35. No material milestone by age 26 is documented.

name: Stephanie Hurlburt
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Birth year is not documented in reviewed sources; public career milestones (Oculus/Unity graphics engineering, co-founding Binomial in 2016) lack a verified ≤26 dated breakout.
early_history_summary: Graphics engineer who worked at Oculus VR and Unity before co-founding Binomial with Rich Geldreich in 2016 to commercialize Basis texture/image compression. Also known for public writing on engineering careers and mental health. Education includes The Evergreen State College per professional profiles.
evidence_summary: Hurlburt is a respected graphics engineer and indie founder, but without a documented birth year or a clearly dated material milestone at or before 26, she cannot be coded as age-26 eligible under the rubric.

name: Justin Kan
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Justin.tv in 2007 at age 23–24 with Emmett Shear, Michael Seibel, and Kyle Vogt, launching a pioneering live video platform (later spinning out Twitch) after earlier YC-backed Kiko Calendar in 2005.
early_history_summary: Born 16 July 1983 in Seattle. Attended Yale University. Joined the first Y Combinator batch in 2005 with calendar startup Kiko, then co-founded Justin.tv in 2007, becoming the public face of lifecasting before the product evolved into a multi-category live video platform and gaming spinout Twitch.
family_context_summary: Born in Seattle; Chinese-American background. Brother Daniel Kan later co-founded Exec with him. Family financial details not richly documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; sibling collaboration with Daniel Kan appears later in Exec.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Y Combinator first batch, Yale, Justin.tv cofounders, Silicon Valley, Paul Graham network
evidence_summary: Kan combined Yale education, the inaugural Y Combinator cohort, and a high-trust cofounder team (Shear, Seibel, Vogt) to launch Justin.tv at ~23–24, creating a live-video platform that later spawned Twitch (Amazon acquisition ~$970M). The early YC network and complementary team were decisive advantages; lifecasting also built unusual personal distribution.
starting_point: Born 16 July 1983 in Seattle, Washington; Chinese-American background; educated at Yale University.
current_position: Entrepreneur and investor; co-founder of Twitch; launched NFT/gaming ventures Fractal (renamed Stash); former Y Combinator partner and Atrium founder; maintains a large YouTube/creator presence.

trajectory.event: Participated in the first Y Combinator batch with calendar startup Kiko.
Co-founded Justin.tv and began high-profile lifecasting that popularized the live video platform.
TwitchTV gaming spinout launched from Justin.tv's most popular category.
Socialcam acquired by Autodesk for about $60 million.
Twitch acquired by Amazon for approximately $970 million; became a Y Combinator partner.
Founded legal-tech firm Atrium (later shut down in 2020 after raising large venture rounds).
Launched Fractal NFT marketplace (later rebranded Stash for game developers).

name: Alexey Dosovitskiy
milestone_by_age_26: No material domain milestone by age 26 found. Earned MSc (2009) and PhD in mathematics/functional analysis (2012) from Moscow State University at ages ~22 and ~25, but the defining CV/ML contributions (e.g., FlowNet, Vision Transformer lead authorship) came after 2013 postdoc work and into the late 2010s–2020.
early_history_summary: Trained as a mathematician at Lomonosov Moscow State University (MSc 2009, PhD 2012 in functional analysis). From 2013–2015 he was a postdoctoral researcher in Thomas Brox's Computer Vision Group at the University of Freiburg, then became a leading deep-learning vision researcher including lead author on Vision Transformer (ViT).
evidence_summary: A mathematics PhD by ~25 is academically strong but not treated here as a material field-defining milestone in computer vision/AI; Dosovitskiy's widely cited breakthroughs (optical flow deep nets, ViT) occurred later. Marked ineligible under a conservative reading of the age-26 rule.

name: Shona Brown
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Approximate birth year c. 1966; Rhodes Scholar and Stanford PhD path, then McKinsey from 1995 (~age 29) and Google SVP from 2003 (~age 37). Book Competing on the Edge (1998) and Google leadership arrived after 26.
early_history_summary: Earned a bachelor's in computer systems engineering from Carleton University, a master's as a Rhodes Scholar at Oxford, and a PhD in industrial engineering/engineering management from Stanford. Joined McKinsey in 1995, made partner, published Competing on the Edge with Kathleen Eisenhardt in 1998, then joined Google in 2003 to build business and people operations.
evidence_summary: Brown's Rhodes Scholarship and elite academic path are impressive, but independently verifiable material professional milestones (McKinsey partnership, HBR Press book, Google SVP) all fall after age 26 under the approximate 1966 birth year.

name: Bob Kahn
milestone_by_age_26: No material career-defining milestone by age 26 found. Earned BSEE from CCNY (1960), MA (1962) and PhD (1964) from Princeton in electrical engineering at ages ~21–25, but ARPANET design work at BBN and TCP/IP with Vint Cerf came in the late 1960s–1970s when he was ~30+.
early_history_summary: Born 23 December 1938 in Brooklyn to an Ashkenazi Jewish family (parents Beatrice and Lawrence Kahn). Completed electrical engineering degrees at City College of New York and Princeton, then worked at Bell Labs and MIT before becoming principal ARPANET designer at BBN and later inventing TCP/IP concepts at DARPA with Cerf.
family_context_summary: Born in Brooklyn to Beatrice Pauline (née Tashker) and Lawrence Kahn in an Ashkenazi Jewish family; related through his father to futurist Herman Kahn.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as domain-proximate to computer networking; family was Jewish professional class in New York.
evidence_summary: Kahn is a tier-1 Internet pioneer (Turing Award, Presidential Medal of Freedom), but his PhD at 25 is education, not a material public milestone comparable to ARPANET demonstrations or TCP/IP. Defining work occurred after age 26.

name: Will Ahmed
milestone_by_age_26: Founded WHOOP in 2012 at age 22 while a Harvard undergraduate and squash captain, building wearable technology focused on recovery and strain rather than step counting; first devices launched 2015.
early_history_summary: Egyptian-American only child who grew up on Long Island playing many sports; attended elite St. Paul's School (NH) and Harvard College (government, class of 2012), captaining men's squash. Inspired by overtraining as an athlete, he read medical literature and founded WHOOP out of Harvard Innovation Labs in 2012 with no prior full-time job.
family_context_summary: Only child raised on Long Island; father is Egyptian immigrant who worked in financial services. Attended expensive elite prep school St. Paul's, indicating substantial family educational investment.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked in financial services after immigrating from Egypt; not sports-tech domain expertise, but provided immigrant professional-class stability.
primary_early_advantage_tags: St. Paul's, Harvard, collegiate athlete domain exposure, Harvard Innovation Labs, athlete early customers
evidence_summary: Ahmed's elite prep-to-Harvard pipeline, multi-sport athletic immersion, and direct lived problem (overtraining as squash captain) produced domain insight that became WHOOP at age 22. Early strategy of seeding elite athletes (Phelps, LeBron) created halo distribution. Family financial services background and St. Paul's tuition point to capital safety for experimentation; founder reports WHOOP was his first full-time job.
starting_point: Egyptian-American only child raised on Long Island, New York; father immigrated from Egypt and worked in financial services; attended St. Paul's School and Harvard.
current_position: Founder and CEO of WHOOP; company valued at multi-billion dollars (reported ~$3.6B in 2021, higher in later reports); TIME100 Sports 2026; Harvard Medical School Board of Fellows.

trajectory.event: Founded WHOOP while a Harvard student and men's squash captain, prototyping recovery-focused wearables.
Launched WHOOP's first commercial wearable device to athletes and teams.
WHOOP reached unicorn status (~$1.2B valuation) with SoftBank and IVP among investors.
Raised further capital valuing WHOOP at about $3.6 billion after SoftBank investment.
Opened Kenmore Square HQ in Boston; named to Harvard Medical School Board of Fellows.
Announced Cristiano Ronaldo as investor/ambassador and expanded into India and Gulf markets.
Named to TIME100 Most Influential People in Sports; continued as WHOOP CEO.

name: Chris Cox
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Facebook in 2005 at age 22–23 as one of the company's first ~15 software engineers after dropping out of a Stanford Symbolic Systems graduate program; helped build News Feed, a defining product surface.
early_history_summary: Born 2 September 1982 in Atlanta and raised in affluent Winnetka, Illinois; attended New Trier High School. Earned a Stanford bachelor's in Symbolic Systems (AI concentration) and began a Symbolic Systems graduate program before leaving to join early Facebook in 2005.
family_context_summary: Youngest of three children raised in Winnetka, Illinois (wealthy Chicago suburb); attended highly regarded New Trier High School. Specific parental occupations not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford Symbolic Systems, early Facebook, Silicon Valley, Winnetka/New Trier
evidence_summary: Cox entered Facebook at ~23 as an early engineer via the Stanford AI/Symbolic Systems pipeline during the social-network structural wave, contributing to News Feed and rising to CPO. Affluent Illinois upbringing and elite high school/university path provided institutional acceleration; family domain transfer is not documented.
starting_point: Born 2 September 1982 in Atlanta; raised in Winnetka, Illinois as youngest of three; attended New Trier High School and Stanford University.
current_position: Chief Product Officer of Meta Platforms (returned 2020 after a 2019 departure); long-time senior product leader overseeing major consumer apps.

trajectory.event: Dropped out of Stanford graduate school to join Facebook as one of the first ~15 software engineers; contributed to News Feed.
Promoted to Chief Product Officer of Facebook.
Given responsibility for Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger product suite.
Left Facebook after disagreement with privacy/messaging pivot strategy.
Returned to Facebook/Meta as Chief Product Officer at Zuckerberg's request.
